messages:
alex: Heads-up — saw a user report where a streaming request that got truncated during a tool call ended up with two provisional charges in the console. Not sure if this is a billing UI duping or ledger double-counting.

maya: Ugh. Any reproducible steps?

alex: Quick repro: initiate stream, trigger a tool_call mid-stream, then force a reconnect while server is still flushing suffix. Console shows provisional charge for original session and another when the reconnect finishes.

tyler: Can you paste the raw router trace? I want to see handoff/session ids.

alex: Paste below (sanitized):

```
router: session=sea-12345 route=west-1 -> nodeA (prefetch)
runtime: toolcall start id=tcall-9 seq=42
runtime: truncated chunk at seq=50 (client reconnect)
router: new session=sea-12345-1 route=west-2 fallback
billing-bot: [provisional-charge] session=sea-12345 tokens=210
billing-bot: [provisional-charge] session=sea-12345-1 tokens=35
```

maya: Looks like the reconnect used a new ephemeral session id but kept the original session tag for metric attribution. That could lead console to show two provisional lines. Does ledger dedupe by client_session or by router_session?

tyler: Ledger dedupe currently keys on confirmed_charge_id; provisional charges are allowed to accumulate until finalization. If both provisional entries were accepted and then finalization produced a single confirmed charge, we'll reconcile — but the console shows both as confirmed in that user's dashboard?

alex: User saw both as confirmed (not provisional) within ~30s. It's either premature finalization or a double-confirm path.

liz: Is this tied to toolcall truncation specifically? We recently changed the toolcall path to return a truncated EOF response when client reconnects during flush. Maybe finalization hook runs on both original and fallback path.

marco: I pushed a tiny repro harness a few mins ago to /eng-platform/stream-repro and can run it against staging. If we can reproduce, we should trace confirmed_charge events from ledger.

alex: I repro'd on staging once. I can share the session token and events.

tyler: For quick triage: add debug logs around charge-finalize in runtime -> router handoff. Specifically log (charge_id, client_session, router_session, confirmed). Something like:

```
TRACE finalize_charge charge_id=%s client_session=%s router_session=%s confirmed=%s
```

liz: Also check toolcall TTL/timeout handling. If the tool path completes and triggers finalize, then reconnect path may call the same finalize again if idempotency isn't enforced.

maya: Good point — are finalize RPCs idempotent? I thought ledger finalization used an at-most-once token but provisional flow doesn't attach it.

tyler: Current flow: provisional charges created by runtime with provisional_id, finalization RPC includes provisional_id -> ledger confirms and returns confirmed_id. If reconnect branch fabricates a new provisional_id because it looks like a fresh request, we can get two confirmed_ids.

marco: So root cause candidate: reconnect branch creates a fresh provisional record instead of reattaching original provisional_id. Two paths both reach finalized state.

alex: That matches the trace — original prov id missing in the second path. Why didn't the router propagate provisional_id across handoff?

liz: Router uses `session_metadata` header to carry provisional_id during normal handoff but there's a special fast-path handoff for toolcall flush that currently omits session_metadata for perf. I was part of that change.

maya: Oof. We optimized a hot path and lost metadata. We should either reattach provisional_id on the fast-path or make finalize idempotent by provisional metadata. Which is lower risk?

tyler: Making finalize idempotent in ledger is safer long-term but larger scope. Quick fix: ensure fast-path copies provisional_id. Patch is small.

liz: I'll open a PR to copy provisional_id in the fast-path and add unit test. Also add a temporary console guard to hide duplicate confirmed_ids from user view while we fix backend.

alex: +1 on both. For console guard, prefer detection: same client_user, overlapping time window, similar prompt hash -> collapse. Keep a flag so we can roll back.

marco: I'll run the staging repro after your patch. If it still duplicates, we escalate to ledger changes.

billing-bot: [note] provisional -> confirmed processing time is ~12s on staging currently. If two provisional records are created within that window, both may be confirmed independently.

tyler: Action items: liz to PR fast-path copy of provisional_id, maya to add console collapse flag, marco to run repro and pipe router/runtime traces into #eng-platform with traces attached. I'll open a ledger follow-up ticket for idempotent finalize.

maya: Filing ticket ENG-1127 for console collapse UX (temporary).

liz: PR up: https://git.internal/redwood/fastpath-provisional-fix (WIP). Tests failing on one edge-case where provisional_id is null — need to nil-check.

alex: Thanks — if we can get a staging green and repro run, I'll reply to the customer. Suggested reply: sorry + we found short-term fix + ETA for patch + mitigation instructions (turn off fast-path in their dedicated cluster?).

marco: Repro run queued, will post results in ~10m.

alex: (thanks) :thumbsup:

marco: Repro confirmed on staging before PR. After liz's patch applied to staging, repro shows single confirmed charge. Posting traces here: https://links.internal/runs/1745204321/repro-trace

maya: Awesome. We'll keep ledger durable idempotency as follow-up but this buys us time.

alex: Closing loop with customer now.

liz: I'll land the PR and backport to the last two releases.

tyler: Add a quick dashboard alert for sudden spike in "confirmed charges per session" so ops can detect similar regressions fast.

maya: Good idea. I'll add an alert panel to the billing dashboard and link it into paging thresholds.

alex: Great teamwork — thanks all.
